Folding `ENTRY` onto the paragraph label line makes it read 1 (micro-repro in #2863) and is deliberately NOT done here: real Enterprise COBOL writes ENTRY on its own line, so folding would buy a green rosetta cell while every real COBOL program kept reading 0. 2026-09-07 (gitgalaxy#2863, engine PR gitgalaxy#2864, merged): the Mode A window gap above is FIXED. cobol routes to `_cobol_args_window_end`, which extends a paragraph's args window across LEADING `ENTRY` statements (blank lines transparent, since prism blanks comment lines in place), so each of the nine planted paragraphs measures args 1 and `avg_func_args` goes 0.0 -> 0.75 (-100% -> -25.0%, IN BAND -- the cell is green and `cobol-entry-args-outside-mode-a-window` is retired with no successor). No value in this manifest moves: verify_language still passes the same 81 assertions, because avg_func_args is a derived bias-report metric, not a planted signal. The fix is ENTRY-only by design -- across the real-world crucible COBOL corpus (570 files, 10155 paragraphs) all 158 paragraphs carrying a USING/RETURNING in their block are CALL invocations (123), the program-level PROCEDURE DIVISION (26) or XML RETURNING clauses (3), none a parameter declaration -- so the real corpus moved by exactly 0 and gitgalaxy's golden masters took a zero diff. TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE TOUCHING THIS LANGUAGE'S FILE SET: (1) avg_func_args is a MEAN PER FILE (main.cbl 0/4 = 0.0; a/b/c 3/3 = 1.0 each; mean 0.75), not corpus args over corpus functions -- the pre-merge prediction of 9/13 = 0.69 was wrong for exactly that reason. (2) 0.75 is EXACTLY the band edge and passes only on a strict `>` comparison, so the margin is 0.00: adding a fifth cobol file, or a paragraph without an `ENTRY`, tips the cell back out of band. main.cbl's four paragraphs cannot cheaply gain one -- screened, four ENTRY lines take main.cbl api 1 -> 5, the trade gitgalaxy#2804 already declined.
